out.text: And any heroes who object can take it up with me. On the roof.
Four districts dark. Half my roster drained. Somebody give me good news.
Good news: the coffee machine survived.
Patch.
Bad news: so did the Redactor.
Can we skip to the part where I'm right? We need more people.
People who aren't scared of him. That's a short list.
Then we make it longer.
Uh. Small thing. Someone's climbing the outside of the Fortress.
Nobody climbs a sixty-storey wall.
Hi! Sorry. Your front door has, like, nine locks.
I'm Volt. I'm a hero. Well... rookie hero. I saw the broadcast, and I want to help.
Oh, I like him.
You're bleeding.
The wall had opinions.
Bastion. Give the rookie a run.
Training roof. Now. Let's see what you've actually got.
Right now? I just climbed sixty floors.
Halo on comms. So you're the rookie everyone keeps talking about.
Halo? THE Halo? Okay. Okay. Be cool. I'm being cool.
You're narrating.
...Yep.
Bastion. I hold this city's line. Tonight, I'm holding yours.
Cool. Great. I'll hold... a different line.
Just hold still and take the gear.
Echo. And before you say anything, I already know how tonight ends.
Do you, though?
...Mostly.
Thorn. I used to be on the other side.
Glad you switched.
Some days, so am I.
Patch. I build the gear. You break the gear.
I'll try to break it less.
You won't. But I appreciate the lie.
Whoa, whoa. Hold up. You're the new kid? They sent the new kid?
I prefer 'rookie'. Sounds more official.
Kid, I've been running furnaces since before you had teeth. You know what happens to things that get too close to the fire?
They... get warm?
They get warm.
Oh, finally. An audience.
I'm here to stop you.
Everyone says that before the first song. Nobody says it after the encore.
Is it a long set?
Darling, it's a residency.
Mind the vines. They bite. Well. They don't bite. They just never let go.
That's somehow worse.
Everything on this roof is slowly becoming mine. The pipes. The rails. You, if you stand still long enough.
Noted. Moving a lot. Got it.
Hi. Over here. No, over here. No, you know what? Pick one. I'll wait.
How about I just hit all of you?
Ooh. Bold. Wrong, but bold.
Picked a bad night to go swimming, rookie.
I didn't really pick it. I kind of just... landed here.
Story of this whole district. Nobody chooses the docks. The docks choose you.
Another one.
Another... what?
Another small, loud hero on my roof. I have carved forty-one names. Yours will be forty-two.
Can you at least spell it right? It's V-O-L-T.
...I will consider it.
Complaint? From who?
Yeah, I'm going to have to decline.
You must be the rookie.
Hi. Yes. That's me. Volt. Huge fan. I mean, hi.
Bastion says you asked to join the roster. I didn't vote for you.
Oh. Okay. That's... fair.
Prove me wrong.
So. You're Volt.
That's me! Hi. Nice table.
Don't touch my table.
I wasn't going to—
Workshop's left. Armoury's right. Gate's at the bottom. My table is in the middle. Don't touch it.
Oh, great. The new one.
Hi! I'm Vol—
Volt. I know. I read your file. I read everyone's file.
You read minds. That's not reading a file.
Potato, potahto.
Hi. I'm—
Thorn. And yes. I was one of them.
I wasn't going to ask.
Everyone asks. Mind the ferns.
Patch. Comms, gear, coffee.
In that order?
Depends on the night. The terminal's for upgrades. Shards go in, a better you comes out.
A better me?
A slightly better you. Let's be realistic.
Good evening. Your heroes have been very brave. I have taken the liberty of making that unnecessary.
Their powers are gone. Do listen carefully. I would hate to repeat the demonstration.
My associates will attend to each district. Stay inside. If you hear someone calling for a hero, let them finish.
Sleep well. I know how much safer you feel when someone else is watching.
Ah, Volt. Such a promising file. And one complaint I would like to discuss in person.
Mine. You have mistaken my patience for permission to enter.
You think the lightning makes you brave. I shall remove it, and we can meet the person underneath.
Of course you are. They all ask to keep something.
A small question, Volt. Before we begin. Indulge me.
Does Halo still stand on that balcony every night? Watching the city. Never looking down.
Ask her who stood beside her. Watch her face when you do.
You are breathing rather well, considering how we left things. Someone has been taking care of you.
I shall remember that. Someone ought to.
Persistence is not a power, Volt. It is simply fear that has not recognised itself yet.
For the moment. I prefer to let a habit establish itself before I correct it.
I flagged your little victory. I have spent the interval learning exactly where you break.
With pleasure. This time, I shall be thorough.
She has not told you. How considerate. She always did know what people could bear.
Halo and I were partners. Then the tower fell. There was time to make one choice. She made it while I was still calling her name.
The city was saved. I was left beneath it. She found the distinction quite manageable.
Redacted. There are things even she does not get to keep.
Because power lets a person decide who is worth saving. I have been on the other side of that decision.
Take it away, and the choosing stops. Every life is equally fragile. Even hers.
Yes. You understand me perfectly.
Halo. I wondered how long you could bear to listen.
Of course. There is always someone else to save while I am speaking.
Twice you have left this room alive. You are beginning to mistake a pattern for a promise.
Some rooms must be kept exactly as they were. She understands why.
I'm not here for you. I'm here for him.
Let's see you move. And no climbing anything.
That dummy's survived forty rookies. Ruin its streak.
Now your Special. Every style's is different. Let's find out what yours does.
Dash. You're untouchable for half a second. Make the half second count.
Watch the white ring. Tap Block as it closes. A parry stops damage, reflects shots, resets your dash and charges Overload. Now catch one.
That took a chunk of his Composure. Strikes chip it away. Parries crush it. Empty the gold bar and he staggers for three seconds. Your hits deal double damage.
Overload's full. Let it rip.
Last ones. Then you're on the clock for real.
Back already? I only just scraped your confidence off the furnace.
Same jacket? Brave choice. It was medium-well when you left.
I remember you. The rookie with the excellent smoke alarm impression.
My favourite returning audience. You spent the last encore on the floor.
You came back! The reviews said my last performance was absolutely flattening.
No need to bow this time, darling. Last time you never got back up.
Oh, you survived the compost heap. Most things come back as tomatoes.
Your little dent in the moss is still here. I kept it watered.
Welcome back. The vines have been asking about their favourite chew toy.
I remember that face. So do all my reflections. We had a lovely laugh.
Back for another look? Last time the floor got most of your attention.
Do try hitting the right one. Watching you lose to my reflection was embarrassing for both of us.
Back again? I've had driftwood put up more of a fight.
You left a lovely Volt-shaped dent on my dock. Mind stepping in it again?
I remember you. All that lightning, and you still went out like a wet match.
I remember you. The roof remembers you. The dent is still there.
Your name is already carved. This saves time.
You return. The stone remains unimpressed.
Volt. You remember the floor, I trust. You were so reluctant to leave it.
I wondered whether you would return. Recovery can do such unkind things to a person's judgment.
You have rehearsed what you will say to me. How touching. Last time, you became very quiet.
